> We run millions of queries on multiple data sources for analytics every day. They run on hive, oracle, druid etc. We needed a way to utilize the data stores in our architecture to exploit them for what they do best. This meant we needed to easily tune and identify sets of use cases where each data store fits the best. Our goal became to build a centralized system which was able to make these decisions on the fly at query time and also take care of the end to end query execution. The system needed to take in all the heuristics available, applying any constraints already defined in the system and select the best data store to run the query. It then would need to generate the underlying queries and pass on all available information to the query execution layer in order to facilitate further optimization at that layer.

A cross build has further requirements; see Cross-compiling.

- On Linux, pgrx's CI generates the C macros with every Clang major from 14 through 23, on x86_64 and aarch64, and requires those versions to generate the same macros. Other Clang versions are not tested on Linux.

- `pgrx-pg-sys` uses the driver to find the target's system headers, to check the C macro profile against the PostgreSQL headers and to compile its native support archive, including the `cshim` feature. Its major version must match `libclang`. pgrx uses `CLANG_PATH` when it is set; otherwise it uses the first match among the `CLANG` recorded in a `pg_config` program's `--configure` output, the `clang` installed with `libclang`, and `clang-<major>` or `clang` on `PATH`.

- The archiver is `llvm-ar` from the driver's LLVM release, or `llvm-lib` for Windows targets. pgrx looks for `llvm-ar-<major>` beside a `clang-<major>` driver, then `llvm-ar` beside the driver or beside its resolved path, such as Debian's `/usr/lib/llvm-<major>/bin/llvm-ar`. Without one, builds for Unix targets use the system `ar`, which works for native builds but may not index objects built for another target.
- A failure to generate the C macros stops the build with an error that names the cause.
- A driver that loads a default configuration file, as Gentoo's Clang does, is refused. Set `CLANG_NO_DEFAULT_CONFIG=1` to build without it.

`GET /health` reports hosting environment, database role, a stable public configuration digest
(`configDigest`) and effective-setting provenance (`configProvenance`). The report uses selected
deployment routers and per-chain commits, with safe names for conflicting overrides.
`DEPLOYMENT_REVISION` is an expected Git commit and never replaces the selected deployment
record. Endpoints are reported only as omitted values and their source; database credentials,
signer material, host/path/process identity and arbitrary metadata are excluded. The digest
covers public effective settings and selected deployment identities, excluding endpoint
credentials, diagnostic-only overrides and tuning for disabled workers. Equivalent explicit
defaults and reordered JSON targets therefore share a digest. Provider health does not
also include an opaque `nextCursor`; pass it back with the same filters for stable keyset
pagination. Cursors are scoped to the descending transfer-id order and reject mismatched filters.
